informal_statement:
Under the same hypotheses \(a\in\mathbb R\),
\[
R>0,
\]

\[
0\leq\theta\leq\pi,
\]
the nonnegative Lebesgue integral of
\[
2\sqrt{R^2-(y-a)^2}
\]
over \([a+R\cos\theta,a+R]\) equals the nonnegative-real embedding of
\[
R^2(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta).
\]
reason: Source `CMVGeometry.lean:1801-1819`: The nonnegative integral and extended-real embedding are distinguished from the preceding ordinary interval integral, with the same angle domain.
